summary: MISO files Tariff revisions in ER26-3650 setting Interconnection Reliability Requirements for Large Loads of 50 MW or more: visibility, PMU, ramp-rate and ride-through rules, with grandfathering for loads in service by December 4, 2026.
ask: Accept the Large Load Interconnection Reliability Requirements Tariff revisions effective December 4, 2026.

points.point: MISO says the filing answers some E-8 concerns (visibility, ramp rate, ride-through) and leaves study, products, cost-shift and proximate generation issues for later filings.
points.quote: proposing visibility, ramp rate, and disturbance ride-through requirements applicable to Large Loads, along with transition provisions to minimize disruption to commercial arrangements.

points.point: Large Load means 50 MW or more at a single substation behind one or more points of withdrawal.
points.quote: Load with Demand of 50 MW or more associated with any facility or aggregation of facilities located at a single substation

points.point: MISO requests a December 4, 2026 effective date.
points.quote: MISO requests that the Tariff revisions submitted herewith be made effective December 4, 2026

points.point: The proposal applies to transmission customers serving the load and covers four categories: visibility, PMU, ramp and ride-through.
points.quote: The proposed framework focuses on four categories of reliability requirements that will be applicable to Large Loads.

points.point: MISO says its study-process enhancements will come in a future section 205 filing.
points.quote: MISO intends to address enhancements to stability assessment study processes in a future Federal Power Act section 205 filing.

points.point: MISO lists further proposals due before the November 16, 2026 abeyance deadline, including LARS for proximate load and a Firm Service Step Up.
points.quote: MISO is refining its Load Addition and Resource Study (“LARS”) process to facilitate the parallel study of load and generation that will address service to proximate load

points.point: Initial ramp limits for Computational Load are 30 MW per minute up and down.
points.quote: MISO is proposing initial up- and down-ramp limits of 30MW/minute.

points.point: Loads with a Service Commencement Date on or before December 4, 2026 are exempt from the new Section 37A for service already procured.
points.quote: MISO proposes to fully exempt, or “grandfather,” any Large Load that has a Service Commencement Date on or prior to December 4, 2026

throughLine.text: MISO's first large-load tariff filing after the E-8 order, covering operational requirements and leaving cost-recovery, transmission products and proximate-generation study for filings due by the abeyance deadline of November 16, 2026.
